translations.translatedText: # Friday 11.9.2020 (radio)

Finland is easing travel restrictions. Swedes are delighted, but Finland's tourism sector hopes for more relief. Finland's new corona figures. Finland takes refugee children from Greece. Rainy weather has spoiled the grain harvest prospects.
## Tourism is being eased

![Minister of Economic Affairs Mika Lintilä, Minister of the Interior Maria Ohisalo and Minister of Transport and Communications Timo Harakka.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11539415)
Open image viewer

Minister of Economic Affairs Mika Lintilä, Minister of the Interior Maria Ohisalo and Minister of Transport and Communications Timo Harakka told about easing the travel restrictions. Photo: Antti Aimo-Koivisto / Lehtikuva

The government is easing travel restrictions. For example, people from Sweden, Norway and Germany can again travel to Finland without a two-week quarantine. The relief comes into force in a week, on Saturday.
Entry is still restricted, however, from countries where there are many coronavirus infections.

Later the restrictions will be eased further, so that people can come to Finland and the quarantine time will be shortened if they take corona tests. If the journey lasts less than 3 days, a pre-test is enough and no quarantine is required.
The relief is meant to help Finnish tourism companies, especially in Lapland.
## Sweden was delighted, Finland's tourism sector was disappointed
![Silja Line in the Eteläsatama harbour in Helsinki.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11431973)
Open image viewer
People in Sweden are delighted that they can come to Finland again. Photo: Petteri Bülow / Yle

The tourism sector says that easing the travel restrictions is a step in the right direction. However, many are also disappointed and hope that the restrictions will be eased even more. In Lapland, for example, there is fear that tourists will not come if they are required to take corona tests.

In Sweden, on the other hand, people are delighted to hear that they can come to Finland again, says Yle's Stockholm correspondent Kirsi Heikel. Many have been waiting to be able to meet relatives and friends in Finland again. Swedes have also missed Finnish tourists, Heikel says.
## The corona situation in Finland
![Corona sign at a Central Finland hospital](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_6016,h_3384,x_0,y_320/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-7148415f507b864d937/1599110515)
Open image viewer
Corona sign at a Central Finland hospital. Photo: Isto Janhunen / Yle
In Finland, 43 new coronavirus infections have been reported today.
During the last two weeks there have been about 130 more corona infections than during the two weeks before.
The number of corona deaths has not grown. A total of 337 people have died of corona.
Refugee children to Finland
## Children from Moria

![Asylum seekers who left the Moria camp on Lesbos on Thursday.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3543,h_1993,x_0,y_183/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-7175335f5a409f63748/1599750368)
Open image viewer
Asylum seekers from the Moria camp on Lesbos. Photo: Orestis Panagiotou / EPA
Finland will take in asylum seekers from the Moria refugee camp in Greece.
Finland will take in 11 children. They have been at the Moria camp without a guardian.
The Moria camp on the island of Lesbos was destroyed in a fire a couple of days ago. 13,000 asylum seekers lived in the camp.
Besides Finland, many other EU countries are also taking in children from the Moria camp.
## Grain harvest prospects
![Oat field in Lapua on 29 August.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-11539304)
Open image viewer
Oat field in Lapua. Photo: Roni Rekomaa / Lehtikuva
The grain harvest prospects are now very bad.
In recent weeks it has rained so much that the harvest has stopped. The heavy rain softens the fields and weakens the quality of the grain.
Grain official Max Schulman says that the total grain harvest may be about 3 million tonnes. That is less than the average of the last 5 years.
